title: BlackRock's IBIT shrank $105 million on Friday, yet its share count is flat since September
dek: IBIT, BlackRock's spot bitcoin fund, cut 2.44 million shares on November 6, about 1,380 BTC. Yet it has slightly more shares than on September 30, so nearly all of its $6.4 billion drop in assets since then came from bitcoin's price.

title: Hyperliquid holds $626 million of open Zcash bets, more than Binance's $556.9 million
dek: On a quiet Sunday, Zcash was the second most traded market on Hyperliquid, ahead of ether. CoinGecko's data shows the on-chain exchange now carries the largest pile of open ZEC futures of any venue.

title: A shark bought $612,100 of OP in one trade. Nine hours later its wallet held no OP
dek: An Optimism wallet DeepSea calls Hold9675 bought 6.03 million OP on Saturday night, about 3% of the token's daily trading. Its page now shows no OP among its holdings.

title: A $216 million bitcoin whale shows a $291,600 weekly loss, but its moves look like loans
dek: DeepSea counts an 82% win rate and a 7-day loss for an Ethereum wallet holding only cbBTC. Its trade list reads like a borrower moving collateral in and out of a lending market.

title: A shark lost $1.64 million on 5,488 trades in 30 days, then bought $155,000 of DEBIT
dek: DeepSea's page for a shark wallet ending in 1f17 shows losses on BNB Chain, Ethereum and Optimism. On Sunday morning it kept trading: gold tokens out, small caps in.

title: One KOL lost $44,400 on Sunday, wiping out 82% of what 31 winning KOLs made
dek: DeepSea's one-day board lists 58 crypto influencers with a result on November 8. Most made money, but Loopierr's single loss pulled the whole group about $20,900 into the red.

title: Russia lets ordinary investors buy only BTC, ETH and USDT, capped at about $3,665 a year
dek: The Bank of Russia's directive 7441-U, published November 6, 2026, names just three assets that non-qualified investors may buy through a broker, with a yearly limit of 300,000 rubles. It enters into force 10 days after publication.

title: Two BNB Chain influencers made 18 of the same memecoin trades within hours. Both are up this week
dek: DeepSea's KOL wallets for kurtz and tech bought and sold the same tokens, in the same direction and within about an hour, over two days. DeepSea counts every closed trade of theirs this week as a win.

title: A $100 million Ethereum shark traded $450 million in 30 days. Its profit: $26,100
dek: Three quarters of the wallet sits in three dollar tokens. In four minutes from 12:30 a.m. ET it bought $340,000 of Ripple's RLUSD, sold $131,000 of LINK and made 18 buys of under $10 each.

title: A shark sold $13.4 million of bitcoin, ether and JCT in minutes. The buyer made 81,836 trades in a month
dek: A BNB Chain wallet that DeepSea shows down $1.75 million in 30 days sold three tokens just after midnight ET and now holds $28.7 million in a dollar token. DeepSea logs the buyer of its ether and JCT as one of the most active wallets it tracks.

title: Is the memecoin easy-money era over? The 12 biggest memecoins sit 44% to 98% below their highs
dek: Traders are arguing about whether memecoins still pay. We skipped the opinions and pulled the numbers: prices against all-time highs, Pump.fun's revenue and the size of the meme market today.

title: 6 crypto projects are giving up their own chains for Solana, Ethereum, Base, Sui and Arc
dek: A table of nine "chain migrations" is going viral. We checked each row against the projects' own posts: six are confirmed, three are not. Here is where each one is going and what its token did since.

title: Rumor vs record: did hackers pay $15 to drain $2.5 billion from Binance in 20 minutes?
dek: Headlines about the Binance hack keep spreading. We checked the most shared claims against Binance's own report, DeepSea's hack tracker and CoinGecko prices. The single-transaction part holds up. The "$15" and "20 minutes" framing misses the story.

title: Harmony's ONE jumped 85% in a day and a half. Trading hit 3.4 times its market value
dek: ONE went from about $0.00106 to $0.00196 on CoinGecko as daily trading rose from about $2 million to $97 million. We could not confirm an official reason for it.

title: One Mantle shark swapped ether tokens 208 times in a day. Its 30-day result: minus $2,400
dek: The wallet traded about $314,000 between WETH and Mantle's staked ether token in 24 hours. After 2,219 closed trades in 30 days, it is slightly in the red.

title: An Ethereum shark was down $159,600 for the month. Two days later it's up $18,100
dek: DeepSea's PnL table shows one wallet's 30-day result swing by $130,000 in less than a day of closed trades, while ether went nowhere for the week. It now has the best 7-day result of any Ethereum shark with a 7-day figure.

title: An Avalanche shark swapped $1.45 million of Aave USDC deposits for Benqi's in two trades
dek: DeepSea logged the switch as both the second-largest net shark buy and the second-largest net shark sell of the day across all chains. The wallet's closed trades in the last 30 days: five, all winners.

title: CYBER jumped 53% in about a day, then gave back 20%. Sharks on Optimism bought $668,000
dek: CoinGecko shows the small-cap CYBER token trading four times its market value in 24 hours, with South Korea's Upbit the busiest market. DeepSea's shark wallets were net buyers on Optimism over a day in which the price fell.

title: DeepSea's top 10 smart money traders: $256 million in weekly profit, then $110 million
dek: The 7-day profit shown for the crash-week winners on DeepSea's boards fell by more than half in 24 hours. The top two influencers' figures halved, and sharks are still down $3.15 million on closed trades.

title: Sharks "sold" $16.31 million of uniBTC on Berachain. CoinGecko saw $591 of trading
dek: DeepSea's live feed logged two wallets moving about 212 uniBTC out on Berachain in 24 hours. One of them is a DEX pool, and CoinGecko counted less than $600 of uniBTC trading worldwide in the same day.

title: Rumor vs record: was Chainalysis hit by AI, and did attackers see case files?
dek: Claims about the Chainalysis breach kept spreading as the company posted its November 6 update. We checked eight of them against Chainalysis's own incident page: two are wrong or out of date, and two have no evidence behind them yet.

title: Ruble token A7A5 still trades on Uniswap 15 months after sanctions, for about $1,500 a day
dek: In August 2025, Treasury sanctioned A7A5's issuer along with Garantex and its successor, Grinex. FinCEN's November 6, 2026, MEXC order put new numbers on all three. Public data shows the token still trades in tiny amounts, but it cannot show the transfers between agents.

title: MEXC's tracked wallets shed $166 million before FinCEN's order. Then MX fell 6%
dek: DeepSea's MEXC wallets fell from $1.08 billion to about $918 million between November 5 and early November 6, before FinCEN moved against the exchange. They have barely moved since, and the data does not show why.

title: FinCEN and the Fed drop the 2020 plan to cut the travel rule threshold to $250
dek: The 2020 proposal would have lowered the cross-border threshold from $3,000 to $250 and written crypto into the definition of "money." FinCEN pulled it on November 6, 2026.

title: Rumor vs record: what viral posts got right and wrong about the U.S. move against MEXC
dek: Posts about FinCEN's MEXC order spread fast on November 6 and 7, 2026. We checked each claim against FinCEN's own order. Most numbers hold up; two points do not.

title: FinCEN cuts MEXC off from U.S. banks over $16.7 billion in likely illicit flows
dek: The U.S. Treasury's FinCEN ordered U.S. financial institutions on November 6, 2026, to stop sending funds to or receiving funds from MEXC Global. The ban starts 30 days after the order runs in the Federal Register.

title: What 9 on-chain analytics tools are built for, from block explorers to compliance suites
dek: Arkham, Nansen, Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Dune, Glassnode, DefiLlama, block explorers and DeepSea all read public blockchain data, but each is built for a different job. Here is what each one does, what is free and who uses it, from each tool's own site.

title: Chainalysis now says login tokens for every user were exposed. All must reset passwords
dek: The crypto tracing firm first said only names and emails were reached. Its latest update says live tokens for every user and password hashes were exposed, and its Reactor and Data Solutions products are still offline.

title: A Nasdaq-listed HYPE holder wants to be a US futures broker. HYPE is down 15% in a week
dek: Nasdaq-listed Hyperliquid Strategies says a subsidiary has applied to become a futures commission merchant, a step toward offering Hyperliquid perps to US customers. It also booked a $620.6 million quarterly profit, nearly all of it paper gains on HYPE.

title: Shorts are paying longs on 21.5% of ether's open futures bets, against 1.4% for bitcoin
dek: CoinGecko's data on 287 bitcoin and ether perp markets shows short sellers paying to hold their bets on 21.5% of ether's open interest, against 1.4% for bitcoin, a day after the sell-off.

title: Hyperliquid holds $14.9 billion in open bets, second only to Binance on CoinGecko
dek: CoinGecko ranks Hyperliquid second of all derivatives exchanges by open interest, about $14.9 billion. Its traders also churn their positions far less than on centralized rivals.

title: Stock and oil bets outtraded crypto on Hyperliquid: $9.96 billion vs. $9.67 billion
dek: CoinGecko's market data for Hyperliquid shows its 165 builder-run markets, almost all on stocks, indexes and commodities, did more volume than its 179 crypto perps as bitcoin fell 5%.

title: The shark that took $10 million out of Aave on Arbitrum put $8.32 million back
dek: A day after one wallet drove an $8.35 million net outflow from Aave's USDC pool, it bought back almost all of it. The 7-day net is now just minus $27,800.

title: One shark sold $2.59 million of LYK. The token's Arbitrum pool holds $396
dek: DeepSea logged big shark selling in two layer 2 tokens, LayerK's LYK and Linea's LINEA. LYK's public markets were far too small to absorb what was counted.

title: Two sharks bought $3.74 million of USD₮0 on Unichain in a day and sold just $75,000
dek: A day after sharks were net sellers of the dollar token on Unichain, two wallets flipped to heavy buying. One of them also bought $4 million on Optimism.

title: Sharks bought $3.08 million of tokenized SpaceX on Arbitrum. Its DEX pool traded $56,000
dek: Two shark wallets kept buying rSPCX and rCRCL, tokens CoinGecko lists as tokenized SpaceX and Circle stock, even as both fell. Almost none of it went through the public pool.

title: Lido lost $1.8 billion in value in a day. Did anyone actually leave?
dek: DefiLlama shows DeFi's biggest protocols shrank 4% to 8% in 24 hours. Compared with CoinGecko prices, most of that looks like falling prices, not withdrawals.

title: Bitcoin fell 5% in four hours. Fees peaked at just 12 sats after a 67-minute wait
dek: mempool.space data shows the November 5 sell-off barely stressed the Bitcoin network. The biggest fee jumps came when blocks were slow, not when panic peaked.

title: Curve's trading volume nearly quadrupled to $831 million as crypto sold off
dek: DefiLlama shows the stablecoin swap venue went from $215 million to $831 million in a day, while total DEX volume rose less than 3% and several big DEXs slowed. Its fees jumped about eightfold.

title: Stablecoin supply shrank $5 billion in six days. USDT fell the most
dek: DefiLlama shows the total supply of dollar stablecoins fell every day from October 30 to November 5, the day bitcoin dropped below $76,000. Tether's USDT supply fell $2.76 billion in a week.

title: Exchange wallets lost $11.45 billion in 18 hours. Mostly price, not withdrawals
dek: DeepSea's exchange list shrank 4.7% as bitcoin fell about 6%. Binance's holdings dropped $6.84 billion, and MEXC fell 15.8%, the steepest among large exchanges.

title: 71 of 100 shark wallets lost money on closed trades in crash week, $5.85 million in all
dek: DeepSea's realized profit table shows large traders came out behind as bitcoin fell. Three wallets made up 63% of the loss, and one Optimism wallet won 3 of 61 trades.

title: Influencer slingoor turned a $686,000 week into $9.38 million as bitcoin fell
dek: DeepSea's 7-day KOL board changed fast in the November 5 sell-off. The top two influencers now hold 91% of the profit shown in the top 100.

title: Bitcoin fell 6%. DeepSea's top 10 smart money traders went from $98M to $256M
dek: In about 18 hours, the 7-day profit of DeepSea's ten best wallets more than doubled. All ten trade perps on Hyperliquid, and the leader alone added $47.9 million.

title: Greece puts a 10% crypto gains tax to a final vote. Staking income would pay 15%
dek: Greece's finance minister brought a bill with dedicated crypto tax rules to a final vote in parliament on November 4. Gains up to 500 euros a year would be tax free.

title: GL1 Org launches with HSBC and JPMorgan on its member list. What will it build?
dek: Global financial institutions have formed the Global Layer One Organisation to push shared rules for tokenized markets. Its site lists HSBC, JPMorgan, MUFG, Forge and Standard Chartered as members. The project began at Singapore's central bank in 2024.

title: Base now aims for five blocks a second. What does the Denim upgrade break for apps?
dek: Base's Denim upgrade was set to switch mainnet from one block every 2 seconds to one every 200 milliseconds on November 5. Anything that counts blocks to measure time now runs 10 times faster.

title: Canary's staked INJ ETF heads to Nasdaq as INJC. Fees will take up to 30% of rewards
dek: Canary's Staked INJ ETF filed its final prospectus on November 4. The fund plans to stake most of its Injective tokens and keep 70% of the rewards. INJ rose 2.5% in a day the rest of the market fell.

title: Bitcoin lost $4,400 in four hours. Why did ETH and XRP fall even harder?
dek: Bitcoin slid from about $80,300 to under $76,000 on November 5, most of it between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. ET. Ether, Solana and XRP dropped 7% to 9%, and the whole crypto market shed about 8% in a day.

title: Trump Media moved 4,259 BTC to Crypto.com from its collateral wallets. A move is not a sale
dek: Two transfers worth about $344 million left wallets that Arkham labels as collateral for Trump Media's $1 billion convertible notes, weeks before holders can ask for their money back.

title: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin lost about $49 million on 17 chains. It says customers lose nothing
dek: Mercado Bitcoin says it contained a security incident on November 2, 2026, and that no customer will lose assets. Chainalysis puts the theft at about $49 million and says close to $9 million has been frozen.

title: Hackers drained French bank Arkéa's own account. It calls a $133 million estimate about right
dek: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed a cyberattack that sent fraudulent transfers out of the bank's own account, possibly into crypto. It denies the attackers came in through Fortuneo and says customer savings are safe.

title: One shark sold $80.5 million of Aave-deposited USDT in an hour. Its 7-day loss: $1.87 million
dek: The Ethereum wallet ending 4312 moved more than $280 million in a day, mostly in and out of Aave. DeepSea's PnL table shows it with the biggest 7-day realized loss it tracks.

title: Seized UK government wallets rank seventh on DeepSea's exchange list, at $3.95 billion
dek: DeepSea's exchange rankings mix trading venues with seized and long-silent wallets, including $574.14 million in failed QuadrigaCX's. Bitfinex ranks second at $31.27 billion, and one Coincheck wallet holds $3.42 billion.

title: Two sharks ran $51.7 million through Aave's USDC pool on Arbitrum. Net $8.35 million out
dek: DeepSea's 24-hour feed shows $30 million of Aave's USDC receipt token sold and $21.65 million bought. One wallet did most of the round trip.

title: Smart money is 15 to 1 long on ether, but only 2 to 1 on Zcash
dek: DeepSea's Long / Short panel shows all seven of its biggest coins leaning long. Ether and NEAR are the most one-sided, while bitcoin carries the largest short bets.

title: A net 16,251 bitcoin flowed onto exchanges in a week. Binance took in the most
dek: DeepSea's dashboard shows a net 1,387 BTC flowed into exchanges in 24 hours, with Binance up 2,479 BTC while Kraken and Bitfinex lost coins.

title: DeepSea's top 10 smart money traders made $98.4 million in a week, all on Hyperliquid perps
dek: The first 41 names on DeepSea's 7-day leaderboard are Hyperliquid perpetual futures traders. The leader made $16.44 million on $208 million of assets.

title: Sharks bought $10.25 million of WLD on Optimism in a day while its price fell 4%
dek: Thirteen big wallets made 240 WLD trades in 24 hours and net bought about $4.31 million. WLD itself fell 4% on CoinGecko.

title: Sharks sold $9.52 million of USD₮0 on Berachain in a day, $3.39 million in the last hour
dek: One busy wallet made 260 shark trades on Berachain, where DeepSea logged 263 in Tether's cross-chain dollar token. A day earlier the 24-hour selling was about a quarter of the size.

title: This week's worst crypto influencer lost $2.84 million and still bets $27.6 million on a fall
dek: DeepSea shows the KOL wallet mk4 on Hyperliquid holding 11 short positions, led by $7.82 million against ether and $7.69 million against bitcoin, while both coins rose overnight.

title: The TRUMP memecoin hit a record low of $1.22. It is now 98% below its January 2025 peak
dek: The Solana token fell 12.6% in two hours on November 4 as trading volume more than quadrupled, CoinGecko's data shows. Its 24-hour volume is now larger than its whole market value.

title: Ether jumped 4.6% in two hours and bitcoin is back above $80,000. Big traders are 86% long
dek: Most of ether's 5.5% daily gain came between 9 and 11 a.m. ET on November 4, CoinGecko's data shows. DeepSea counts $3.35 billion in long bets against $543.87 million in shorts.

title: 177 crypto influencers made money in 30 days. Four others lost $19.8 million
dek: DeepSea's 30-day KOL leaderboard looks like a winning month: 177 of 202 accounts are up. Then you reach the bottom, where Machi Big Brother alone shows minus $12.42 million.

title: The top crypto influencer of the week made $8.84 million and now sits on $25.5 million in USDC
dek: DeepSea's KOL leaderboard puts "2 freres 2 fauves" first by a wide margin, three times the runner-up. Its latest Hyperliquid orders were in silver and copper markets, not crypto.

title: One Monad wallet bought $2.38 million of ether. Its closed trades lost $1.15 million in 30 days
dek: Every shark trade DeepSea logged on Monad in the last 24 hours came from one wallet. It bought wrapped ether and sold fixed-yield dollar tokens.

title: Shark wallets sold $7.85 million of the USD₮0 dollar token on Optimism, a day after buying it
dek: A day ago shark wallets were buying USD₮0 on Optimism. DeepSea's feed now shows them net sellers of almost $3 million, while OP selling kept going.

title: Binance's 7-day flow on DeepSea: a $1.55 billion net outflow after last week's $5.04B inflow
dek: Last week's DeepSea report showed money pouring into Binance. Its live seven-day count now shows $4.54 billion leaving and $3.00 billion arriving.

title: MEXC took in a net $107.6 million in seven days, more than any other exchange
dek: Among the exchanges DeepSea tracks, MEXC topped the seven-day inflow table while OKX, Gate, Bybit and Bitget all saw net outflows.

title: Robinhood's $14.9 billion ranks third on DeepSea. One cold wallet holds $11.27 billion of it
dek: DeepSea's exchanges list puts Robinhood's labeled wallets behind only Binance and Bitfinex. A single Bitcoin cold wallet holds about three-quarters of the total.

title: Sharks bought $850,000 of Arbitrum's ARB in a day. Whales added $4.59 million in a week
dek: DeepSea's data shows big wallets buying ARB on Arbitrum while $11.6 million more ARB left exchanges than arrived over seven days. Two stock tokens also drew shark money.

title: DeepSea tagged 2,790 new smart money wallets in a week, and not a single new bot
dek: DeepSea's weekly report counts 2,615 wallets seen for the first time from October 26 to November 1, plus 652 new DeFi borrowers and 93 new influencer (KOL) wallets. Here is what the labels mean.

title: OKX logged three times Binance's transfer count last week and lost a net $241.6 million
dek: DeepSea's exchange data shows 451,046 transfers at OKX from October 26 to November 1, with almost twice as many withdrawals as deposits. Bybit went the other way, with a net $478.2 million coming in.

title: Asia's local exchanges handled just 1.3% of flows as Binance took in a net $5.04 billion
dek: South Korea led the local markets with $12.5 million net in. Upbit, HashKey, Bitkub and other home-market exchanges together handled about $538 million of deposits and withdrawals from October 26 to November 1, DeepSea's data shows.

title: Shark wallets sold $3.55 million of Optimism's OP in a day and bought just $486,000
dek: DeepSea's live feed shows big wallets selling Optimism's token while still parking dollars on the chain. On Berachain, a heavy seller of USD₮0 turned buyer in the last hour.

title: MachiBigBrother opened $145,405 of ETH longs in 25 seconds, six hours after the last burst
dek: DeepSea's live feed caught the crypto influencer opening six ether long positions on Hyperliquid at 6:33 a.m. ET, after nine more just past midnight.

title: 32,175 crypto addresses are on DeepSea's risk list. Ransomware is the biggest category
dek: DeepSea's database of scam, fraud and sanctioned addresses grew by 1,178 last week. Most new entries were hack-tainted, and Bitcoin holds more flagged addresses than Ethereum.

title: Whales sent out $317 million more than they took in last week. Where did it go?
dek: DeepSea's wallet-to-wallet map shows $1.10 billion leaving whale wallets and $783 million coming back, while unlabeled wallets pushed a net $306 million into exchanges.

title: Two Hyperliquid wallets are up $20.7 million on open bets. The crowd is down $2.19 million
dek: DeepSea's weekly data names the biggest paper winners on Hyperliquid, a 40x bitcoin short opened on October 31, and an ether short now 3.3% from forced closing.

title: Crypto influencers made $590,000 in 30 days. Sharks in DeepSea's live feed lost $10.7 million
dek: DeepSea's 30-day realized profit table puts its live-feed KOL wallets in the green and shark wallets deep in the red. On Hyperliquid, one KOL opened a $538,000 silver short in nine minutes.

title: Whales put $63 million into stablecoins and sold a net $27.6 million of other tokens
dek: DeepSea's sector data shows big wallets moving into dollars last week, while smart money kept buying. Ethereum took most of the $66 million net inflow.

title: Only 29 of 59 tracked BSC wallets made money last week. Smart money won, influencers lost
dek: DeepSea's weekly data shows BSC smart money wallets finished $7,800 up while eight tracked KOLs lost $55,400. One influencer wallet had no green day in seven.

title: The CFTC cleared perpetual futures on US stocks. Cboe and Citadel filed legal action that day
dek: On November 3, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said perpetual futures on single US stocks can trade on CFTC-registered exchanges for the first time. The same day, Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets Association took legal action to stop it.

title: Sharks bought $3.05 million of WLD on Optimism in a day. One Monad wallet traded $15.7 million
dek: DeepSea's live feed shows big wallets loading up on USD₮0 and WLD on Optimism, one wallet churning $15.7 million on Monad and a single $10 million Aave USDC exit on Arbitrum.

title: One Tron wallet moved $751 million of USDT through Binance in about two hours
dek: DeepSea's list of the week's largest exchange transfers is all dollar tokens: $2.49 billion in 11 moves, led by Coinbase USDC and a single unlabeled Tron address moving USDT to and from Binance.

title: Whales and smart money put $3 million into ZAMA as it fell 14% in a week
dek: ZAMA drew the heaviest combined buying in DeepSea's weekly data, with coins moving to cold storage. Two USD.AI tokens, CHIP and sUSDai, came next.

title: DeFi lenders supplied $12.7 billion in a week. Morpho Blue had 84% of liquidations
dek: DeepSea's lending data for October 26 to November 1 shows deposits far ahead of withdrawals, borrowing almost exactly matched by repayments, and $12.69 million liquidated, most of it on Morpho Blue.

title: Whales cut $28.9 million of LBTC in a week. Smart money bought just $127,900
dek: Lombard's bitcoin token on Ethereum was the most sold token in DeepSea's weekly data, by a wide margin. Whales also cut $6.47 million of ARB, with DeepSea flagging moves to cold storage.

title: PEPE and SHIB flowed into US and European exchanges as $120 million in bitcoin left
dek: DeepSea's weekly data shows Western exchanges nearly flat overall, at minus $54.98 million. Under the surface, memecoins were deposited, bitcoin was withdrawn, Kraken lost 1,526 BTC and one $399.78 million USDC transfer left Coinbase.

title: 448 of 617 Solana influencers lost money last week. The best one won all seven days
dek: DeepSea's tracked crypto influencers on Solana closed the week $395,600 down. A trader called zeropnl made $82,900 with seven green days, while one smart money wallet lost $1.81 million in a single day.

title: Hyperliquid's big traders bet $3.78 billion on a drop. One put $126 million on HYPE rising
dek: DeepSea's tracked traders held six dollars of shorts for every dollar of longs last week. Against that tide, one wallet opened a $126.62 million HYPE long, and a 40x bitcoin bet sat 2.4% from liquidation.

title: $255 million in USDT left Asian exchanges in a week. Gold tokens, USDe and RLUSD moved in
dek: DeepSea's weekly data shows Asian exchanges losing USDT and USDT0 while tokenized gold and smaller dollar tokens arrived. In the last 24 hours, one shark wallet traded $47.8 million of RLUSD on Ethereum.

title: Binance took in a net 66,386 bitcoin, worth $5.2 billion, in the week it was hacked
dek: DeepSea's data shows a net $5.04 billion flowing into Binance from October 26 to November 1, almost all of Asia's net inflow. Who sent it? The data cannot say.

title: $307 million in hack-linked bitcoin hit exchanges in one week. OKX got the biggest share
dek: DeepSea counted 680 deposits of tainted funds into exchanges from October 26 to November 1, nearly all in BTC. OKX took $139.96 million in just 55 of them, including a run of near-identical $15.47 million transfers.

title: A fake job interview opened the door to Binance's $6.34 billion hack, its own report says
dek: Binance's first incident report traces the October 29 theft to a staged hiring process, a poisoned coding test and a developer tool swapped for malware. Then nine minutes of hot-wallet transfers did the rest.

title: 2026's biggest airdrops: $809 million claimed, 9 of 11 tokens below first close
dek: On-chain data compiled by Bitquery puts 51 large EVM airdrops this year at $809.4 million and 2.02 million claiming wallets. Most claimers moved their tokens within a day, and CoinGecko prices show only Backpack and Espresso above their first daily close.

title: Backpack gave users 25% of BP and insiders nothing. BP is up 285% from its first close
dek: Backpack airdropped 250 million BP to points holders and Mad Lads owners on March 23, 2026, worth about $57 million at CoinGecko's first daily close. No team or investor tokens unlocked, and the next 37.5% of supply unlocks only when the company hits growth milestones.

title: MegaETH's MEGA is down 73% since launch. Who really got the 15% 'community' share?
dek: MegaETH launched MEGA on April 30, 2026, after hitting the first of four network milestones. At least a third of its 15% community allocation was sold at auction, MegaETH has not said how much was given away free, and 53% of supply still waits on future milestones.

title: 82,671 wallets claimed Brevis' BREV airdrop. 45% of the claim pot was never collected
dek: Brevis opened its BREV claim on January 6, 2026, after a points campaign, a Kaito leaderboard and a Binance HODLer drop. The Ethereum claim contract still holds 45% of its 20 million BREV, and the token trades about 77% below its first daily close.

title: Jupuary 2026 never landed: 75% of JUP votes shelved a 700 million JUP airdrop
dek: Jupiter's yearly airdrop was due to start with 200 million JUP in early 2026. Stakers voted on February 22 to park all 700 million tokens in a locked community wallet instead. No new vote has been called since, and JUP now trades about 41% above its close that day.

title: Polymarket has no POLY token. So why is it still pursuing a POLY trademark?
dek: Polymarket's help center says it has announced no airdrop and no token launch, and that all rewards are paid in pUSD. Meanwhile a February application to trademark "POLY" for crypto token services is still alive, with a reply filed on November 2.

title: MetaMask's points season ended in LINEA allocations. It has "no plans" for a MASK token
dek: MetaMask Rewards Season 1, from October 28, 2025, to January 23, 2026, gave users above 1,000 points a LINEA allocation. LINEA now trades about 28% below its price on February 23, when MetaMask said the claim window had closed, and the help center says there is no $MASK token plan and no next season, only short campaigns paid in mUSD.

title: What is a rug pull? How crypto exit scams work and 6 warning signs to check
dek: A rug pull is when a project's own insiders take buyers' money and walk away, by draining the pool, printing tokens through a backdoor or dumping their supply. Most of the warning signs are public on-chain before you buy.

title: What is a gas fee? How Ethereum fees work, who gets paid and why they spike
dek: A gas fee is what you pay Ethereum to run a transaction: gas used times the base fee plus an optional tip. The base fee is burned, the tip goes to the validator, and the price can climb 12.5% a block when the network gets busy.

title: Thailand crypto rules explained: licenses, the Bybit and OKX blocks, and tax
dek: Any crypto exchange, broker or dealer serving people in Thailand needs a Thai SEC license, and since April 2025 offshore platforms with Thai features can be blocked. Bybit, OKX and three others were named for blocking from June 28, 2025. Here is what that means for users, payments and tax.

title: What is TON? Telegram's blockchain explained, and why Toncoin is now Gram
dek: TON (The Open Network) is a proof-of-stake blockchain wired into Telegram, with a wallet built into the messenger. Its coin, long called Toncoin, now trades as Gram (GRAM), and that rename is the first thing a new user can trip over.

title: Compound's fourth retreat in a month: a vote to pull 90 ETH and 42,000 USDC off Unichain
dek: A Compound DAO vote closing November 3, with no votes against so far, would send reserves from its deprecated Unichain markets back to Ethereum. A bigger 534,530 USDT withdrawal from Polygon was filed and canceled within an hour.

title: Polymarket adds 15-minute gold and silver bets. One early window traded just $100
dek: Polymarket has added 15-minute and one-hour Up or Down markets on gold and silver, settled by Chainlink price streams. The format began with crypto, where Chainlink says it has passed $9 billion in volume, but the metal markets start almost empty.

title: What is Bitcoin? How it works, why only 21 million exist and the risks
dek: Bitcoin is a digital currency that moves directly between users on a public network, with no bank or company in the middle. Miners secure it with computing power, its supply is capped at 21 million coins, and BTC traded near $77,323 as of November 2, 2026.

title: A7A5 stablecoin network moved $179 billion. FinCEN wants US banks and crypto firms out
dek: A Treasury proposal would bar about 347,926 US financial institutions, crypto exchanges included, from moving money for the Russia-linked A7 network's front companies. Public comments close November 4, 2026.

title: What is staking? How proof-of-stake rewards work and how you can lose money
dek: Staking means locking tokens to help run a proof-of-stake blockchain, in return for rewards paid in that token. The stake is collateral: validators that go offline lose a little, and on Ethereum those that break the rules can be slashed.

title: What is Chainlink? How DeFi gets its prices, plus CCIP and LINK staking
dek: Smart contracts cannot see the outside world, so lending apps rely on oracles like Chainlink to tell them what ether is worth. Chainlink also moves tokens between chains through CCIP, and LINK pays and backs the node operators who do the work.

title: What is Ethereum? How the global computer works, what ETH does and the risks
dek: Ethereum is a public blockchain that runs programs called smart contracts, and ether (ETH) is the coin that pays for using it and secures it through staking. It launched in July 2015, switched from mining to proof of stake on September 15, 2022, and ETH traded near $2,267 as of November 2, 2026.

title: What is MEV? How sandwich bots profit from your swap, and how to cut the risk
dek: MEV, or maximal extractable value, is the profit made by choosing which transactions go into a block and in what order. Some of it keeps prices in line across exchanges. Sandwich attacks take it straight out of ordinary traders' swaps.

title: What is TRON? How the chain holding $92.6 billion of USDT really works
dek: TRON is the blockchain where more of Tether's USDT lives than anywhere else: about $92.6 billion on November 2, 2026, per DefiLlama. Here is how its energy and bandwidth fees work, and why 27 elected block makers decide the rules.

title: Arbitrum vote could unfreeze Stylus Rust contracts, but each needs an audit and sign-off
dek: New Stylus contracts on Arbitrum have been frozen since October 2 over fears of AI-assisted attacks. A DAO poll closing November 5 weighs a way back: every new program would need an auditor's pass and an Arbitrum Foundation signature.

title: Send USDC on 12 blockchains, get dollars: OnePay adds Stripe-powered checking deposits
dek: Since October 30, 2026, select US OnePay customers can send USDC from an outside wallet straight into OnePay Checking. Stripe's Bridge converts it to dollars with no conversion fee at launch, but the coins are not FDIC insured on the way in.

title: What is the XRP Ledger? How XRP works with no mining, and what Ripple holds
dek: The XRP Ledger has run since 2012 and settles a new ledger every 4 to 6 seconds without mining. XRP is its coin, Ripple is a company that does not own it but reported holding 37.66 billion XRP at midyear, and RLUSD is Ripple's stablecoin on it.

title: Kenya's crypto grace period ends November 4: KSh 25 million fines for unlicensed firms
dek: Crypto firms already serving Kenya had one year to get licensed under the new VASP Act, and that year ends Wednesday. From November 4, 2026, a company operating without a license risks a fine of up to KSh 25 million.

title: Token unlocks November 2 to 8: $1.05 billion due, led by HYPE, and Kite's float jumps 27%
dek: Five scheduled unlocks this week add up to about $1.05 billion at November 2 prices, according to CoinGecko's calendars. Hyperliquid's HYPE is almost 80% of the dollar total, but Kite's KITE release is the biggest relative to what already trades.

title: What is BNB Chain? Three chains, 21 block makers and 0.45-second blocks
dek: BNB Chain is three blockchains that all run on BNB: BNB Smart Chain (BSC) for apps, the cheaper layer 2 opBNB and the storage network Greenfield. Its speed comes from a small club: just 21 validators make BSC's blocks at any one time.

title: Circle and ACI want banks to settle in USDC on rails they already run. First: Colombia
dek: ACI Worldwide, which built the core of Colombia's Bre-B instant payment system, will plug Circle's USDC into its payments platform for a Colombian pilot. The two companies gave no volumes, no bank names and no launch date.

title: BNB just burned $1.2 billion of itself. Why is 100 million still years away?
dek: The 37th quarterly auto-burn destroyed 1,646,196 BNB on October 19, the most coins of any burn this year. Supply is now 131.5 million BNB, still 31.5 million above the long-term target.

title: bStocks, a Binance affiliate's stock tokens, jumps 53% to $1.31 billion and No. 1
dek: bStocks, issued on BNB Chain by a Binance group affiliate, is now the largest tokenized stock platform. By our math it added more value in 30 days than the whole $3.58 billion market did, because the rest of the market shrank.

title: Zcash NU7 makes blocks 3x faster around November 5. Old nodes will split off
dek: Zcash's NU7 hard fork activates at block 3,543,405, expected around November 5, 2026. It cuts block time from 75 to 25 seconds without changing supply, sends 60% of fees to a reserve and invalidates version 4 transactions. Nodes that do not upgrade split off.

title: How stolen crypto is traced and frozen, and why thieves dump stablecoins fast
dek: Every blockchain transfer is public, so investigators can follow stolen funds hop by hop. Money can be stopped in two places: stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle can freeze tokens on-chain, and exchanges can lock accounts when stolen funds arrive.

title: Crypto travel rule explained: what exchanges must send with your transfer
dek: The travel rule requires crypto exchanges and other providers to send the sender's and recipient's details along with a transfer, as banks do with wires. In the EU it applies to every crypto transfer regardless of amount, and 83% of jurisdictions surveyed by the FATF have passed travel rule laws.

title: Dubai VARA crypto rules explained: who needs a license and what it covers
dek: In Dubai, crypto businesses need a license from the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA), which covers the emirate's mainland and free zones except the DIFC. VARA licenses seven activities, from exchanges to custody, and regulates token issuance and crypto marketing.

title: Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep at a record 70%. Did a fake pollster move the odds?
dek: Two days before the November 3 vote, Kalshi's market priced Democrats winning both chambers at 70%, up more than 9 points in a month. Ten days earlier, Kalshi had to explain why a fabricated pollster barely moved its election markets.

title: Stablecoins explained: USDT vs. USDC, the two coins that hold 87% of the market
dek: Stablecoins are tokens built to stay worth $1, backed by reserves such as cash and short-term US government debt. As of November 2, 2026, Tether's USDT ($178.48 billion) and Circle's USDC ($70.68 billion) made up about 87% of a $285.89 billion market, per rwa.xyz.

title: What is Sui? The object-based blockchain that says it settles in 390 ms
dek: Sui is a layer-1 blockchain from Mysten Labs, founded by former Meta engineers, that launched in May 2023. It stores everything as objects with clear owners, runs smart contracts in Move and, by Sui's own figure, settles transactions in roughly 390 milliseconds. SUI has a 10 billion total supply.

title: Copy trading explained: how it works, what lead traders take and why results differ
dek: Copy trading lets you automatically mirror another trader's positions on an exchange, in return for a share of any profit. Your results can differ from theirs because of order size, slippage and timing, and regulators warn it can encourage herd behavior and frequent trading.

title: Seed phrase and hardware wallet safety: the words that guard your crypto
dek: Your seed phrase is the master key to your wallet: anyone who sees it can take everything, and if you lose it, nobody can restore it. A hardware wallet keeps keys offline, but only if the phrase stays offline too and the device is genuine.

title: What is DeepSea (desea.io)? The onchain app that labels wallets and tracks flows
dek: DeepSea (desea.io) is a web app that labels crypto wallets and tracks what smart money, influencers, whales, exchanges and hackers do onchain. It is run by DeepTek Ltd, and its own terms say the data is information only, not financial advice.

title: Japan crypto rules explained: FSA registration, 95% cold storage and 2x leverage
dek: Crypto exchanges in Japan must register with the Financial Services Agency under the Payment Services Act, keep at least 95% of customer coins offline, and cap retail leverage at 2x. A 2026 government bill would revise the rules again, borrowing from securities law.

title: Bored Apes are down 96% from their record. Which NFT blue chip fell least?
dek: Most of the famous NFT collections now sit about 90% to 99% below their peak floor prices in ETH, and the marketplaces are closing. CryptoPunks are the exception, at about 76% down.

title: Stellar votes on Bell November 3: wallets must learn a new "W" address
dek: Stellar's Protocol 30 upgrade, Bell, faces a testnet validator vote on November 3 and a mainnet vote on November 23, 2026. It adds a new "W" address, post-quantum signature checks for smart contracts and millisecond ledger timing, and Stellar says apps must update their SDKs.

title: Bitcoin mining and hashrate explained: difficulty, hashprice and data sources
dek: Bitcoin miners race to find a block hash below a target, and every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) the network resets the difficulty so blocks keep coming about every 10 minutes. Hashrate, the total guessing power, cannot be measured directly; it is estimated from difficulty and block times.

title: What are exchange tokens? BNB keeps burning, OKB froze its supply at 21M
dek: Exchange tokens are coins tied to a crypto exchange that give holders perks on the platform and pay gas on the exchange's own blockchain. BNB shrinks through quarterly burns toward 100 million; OKB's supply was fixed at 21 million in 2025. Both stay tied to one company.

title: What is address poisoning? The copy-paste scam hiding in your wallet history
dek: Address poisoning is a scam where an attacker plants a lookalike address in your transaction history and waits for you to copy it. No hacking is needed, only a tiny or fake transfer and a hurried user, and the payment cannot be reversed.

title: Crypto taxes in the US: Form 1099-DA explained, from proceeds to cost basis
dek: Form 1099-DA is the IRS form US crypto brokers use to report your sales. It shows gross proceeds for sales from 2025 and adds cost basis for certain sales from 2026, but you must report all crypto gains and income whether or not you get one.

title: South Korea crypto rules explained: cold wallets, bank-held cash and jail terms
dek: Crypto exchanges in South Korea must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit and, since July 19, 2024, follow the Virtual Asset User Protection Act: customer cash held at banks, most coins in cold wallets, and prison terms for market manipulation.

title: FDV vs market cap: how to read a token's supply, with HYPE's 4x gap as a guide
dek: Market cap is price times the tokens circulating today. Fully diluted valuation (FDV) is price times the whole supply, including locked tokens. The gap between them shows how much supply is still to come.

title: How to check and revoke token approvals before an old one drains your wallet
dek: Look up your wallet address in an approval checker such as Etherscan's Token Approvals page or Revoke.cash, find spenders you no longer use or do not recognize, and revoke them. Each revoke is an on-chain transaction, so it costs a small network fee.

title: CEX vs DEX explained: who holds your crypto, and what can go wrong
dek: A centralized exchange (CEX) is a company that holds your coins and matches orders in an order book; a decentralized exchange (DEX) is blockchain software that lets you swap from your own wallet against a pool of tokens. The real trade-off is custody: convenience and support on one side, control and responsibility on the other.

title: What is a layer 2? Rollups, proofs and why no big L2 is Stage 2 yet
dek: A layer 2 is a separate blockchain that runs transactions cheaply and settles them on Ethereum, using fraud proofs or validity proofs to show its state is correct. L2BEAT tracks about $30 billion in L2s, and its Stages show how much control each team still holds.

title: One address, two exchange hacks: DeepSea traces where this fall's stolen crypto went
dek: DeepSea says funds from the Bitget and Binance thefts landed at the same address. Its tracker also shows how little of the loot has reached exchanges, and how much is simply sitting still.

title: Prediction markets explained: how Kalshi and Polymarket work, and the real risks
dek: A prediction market lets people trade contracts that pay $1 if an event happens and $0 if it does not, so prices read like odds. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated US exchange; most Polymarket markets settle on chain through the UMA oracle.

title: Singapore crypto rules explained: who needs a MAS license, and who won't get one
dek: Crypto firms serving customers in Singapore need a license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, mainly under the Payment Services Act 2019. Since June 30, 2025, Singapore firms that serve only overseas customers also need a license, and MAS says it will generally not grant one.

title: Crypto options expiry and max pain explained: what happens at 3 a.m. ET
dek: Crypto options on Deribit, a major options exchange, expire at 3 a.m. ET (4 a.m. ET during daylight saving time) and settle in cash against a 30-minute average of an index price. Max pain is the strike price at which the most option value would expire worthless, a number traders watch but one that does not control the price.

title: Token unlocks explained: cliffs, vesting and why unlocked does not mean sold
dek: A token unlock is when tokens locked at launch, usually for the team, investors or a treasury, become free to move. Unlocks add to circulating supply and dilute holders, but an unlocked token is not a sold one: Hyperliquid insiders claimed far less HYPE than they could.

title: What is a wallet drainer? How one signature can empty your crypto wallet
dek: A wallet drainer is a scam kit that tricks you into signing an approval or permit that lets the attacker move your tokens. Your seed phrase never leaves your hands: your own signature does the damage, sometimes days later.

title: Bitcoin dominance and crypto market cap explained: why sites say 58% or 60%
dek: Total crypto market cap adds up the market value of every tracked coin, and bitcoin dominance is bitcoin's share of it. As of November 2, 2026, the total was about $2.6 trillion to $2.7 trillion and bitcoin's share about 58% to 60%, depending on the data site.

title: Hong Kong crypto licensing explained: SFC exchange rules, 2 of 36 stablecoin bids
dek: In Hong Kong, crypto exchanges need a license from the Securities and Futures Commission, and anyone issuing a fiat-backed stablecoin needs one from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Only two stablecoin issuers had been licensed as of April 2026: HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial.

title: SEC vs. CFTC: who regulates crypto in the US, and where the line now falls
dek: The SEC oversees crypto that counts as a security, and the CFTC oversees commodities like bitcoin and ether plus derivatives on them. Since March 2026, the two agencies share an interpretation that says most crypto assets are not securities.

title: Binance Launchpool and HODLer Airdrops explained: how BNB holders earn new tokens
dek: Launchpool pays a new token hour by hour to people who lock BNB or stablecoins; HODLer Airdrops pay one after the fact to people who held BNB in Simple Earn during a past window. Both depend on your share of a pool, and both carry price risk.

title: Ethereum roadmap explained: Pectra, Fusaka and why Glamsterdam has no date
dek: Ethereum upgrades through named hard forks. Pectra went live on May 7, 2025, and Fusaka on December 3, 2025. Glamsterdam, the next one, is live on the Sepolia testnet but was pulled from Hoodi in October 2026, and as of November 2, 2026, it has no mainnet date.

title: Tokenized Treasuries explained: BUIDL, USDY and the $14.2B T-bill market
dek: Tokenized Treasuries are blockchain tokens that stand for shares in funds holding US government debt, and unlike most stablecoins they pay interest. As of November 2, 2026, rwa.xyz counted $14.21 billion across 119 products, led by Ondo's USDY, Circle's USYC and BlackRock's BUIDL.

title: What is a TGE? Token launch day explained, and why most supply stays locked
dek: A TGE, or token generation event, is the moment a crypto project creates its token and the first slice starts to circulate. Airdrop claims and trading usually begin then, while team and investor tokens stay locked for months or years.

title: Bitcoin halving explained: what it is, when the next one is and why it matters
dek: The bitcoin halving is a rule in bitcoin's code that cuts the reward for mining a new block in half every 210,000 blocks, about every four years. The last one happened on April 20, 2024, at block 840,000. The next is due at block 1,050,000, expected around spring 2028.

title: How crypto exchange hacks happen: the weak spot is rarely the key itself
dek: Most exchange hacks start in hot wallets, the online wallets that pay out withdrawals. Attackers rarely break the cryptography. They get into the systems and people that approve transactions, then rush to swap stablecoins before issuers can freeze them.

title: Binance took in 18,435 BTC in two weeks while $6.81 billion in stablecoins walked out
dek: DeepSea's data shows about $1.5 billion in bitcoin flowing into Binance in early October, just as billions in USDT left. Kraken saw the opposite, and the price fell anyway.

title: Doppler's XDP is trending again, with daily volume 95% below launch week. What is it?
dek: Doppler Finance's XDP token sat fourth on DeepSea's 24-hour trending list late on November 1 (ET), a month after launch. CoinGecko shows it hit a record low on October 30, and DeepSea finds the top 10 wallets hold 95% of supply.

title: Vietnam crypto law explained: 5 licenses, VND 200M fines and a 6-month clock
dek: Crypto is legally defined in Vietnam, and a five-year pilot lets up to five licensed local firms run crypto markets. As of the latest official update on October 6, 2026, no provider had been licensed, so the six-month countdown for investors using unlicensed platforms has not started.

title: What is restaking? EigenLayer explained, from extra rewards to slashing risk
dek: Restaking lets stakers put the same stake to work securing extra services for extra rewards. EigenLayer is the main protocol for it: stakers deposit assets, operators run the services, and those services can slash stake when rules are broken.

title: How crypto liquidations work: why a 10% move can wipe out a 10x trade
dek: A liquidation is when an exchange force-closes a leveraged trade because losses have eaten through the trader's collateral. It protects the exchange and other traders from debts the trader cannot pay.

title: AI agents in crypto explained: how bots get wallets and pay, and what can go wrong
dek: An AI agent is software that takes actions on its own, not just answers questions. In crypto, agents hold wallets and pay for things in stablecoins, often through the x402 protocol, with spending limits their owners may or may not switch on.

title: What are points programs in crypto? How they work and why points are not tokens
dek: A points program scores what users do on a crypto product, such as deposits, trades or referrals, and usually hints that points will later become tokens. Points are not tokens: the project decides if, when and how they convert.

title: What is Solana? Alpenglow explained, from 12.8-second finality to a 150 ms goal
dek: Alpenglow is Solana's new consensus protocol. Its first part, Votor, went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, replacing TowerBFT and cutting the time for a transaction to become final from about 12.8 seconds to a target of about 150 milliseconds.

title: CLARITY Act explained: what the crypto market bill would do and why it stalled
dek: The CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633, would write into law which crypto assets and platforms the SEC oversees and which fall to the CFTC. As of November 2, 2026, it is stuck in the Senate after a 49 to 50 vote to start debate failed on September 15.

title: Perpetual futures funding rates explained: how 0.05% can cost 55% a year
dek: A funding rate is a small payment that traders of perpetual futures make to each other to keep the contract's price close to the real market price. When it is positive, longs pay shorts. When it is negative, shorts pay longs.

title: What is Sky Protocol and USDS? The former MakerDAO and its 3.80% savings rate
dek: Sky is the protocol formerly known as MakerDAO. It issues USDS, a dollar stablecoin, and sUSDS, a savings token that earned the Sky Savings Rate of 3.80% shown on Sky.money on November 2, 2026, a rate set by vote and not guaranteed.

title: How crypto airdrops work, and how to spot the scams that copy them
dek: An airdrop is a free drop of tokens to wallets, usually as a reward for early users. Real airdrops never ask for your seed phrase. Most scams instead trick you into signing a transaction on a fake claim site.

title: What is a bitcoin ETF? How spot funds hold coins and what daily flows mean
dek: A spot bitcoin ETF is a fund that holds real bitcoin and trades on a stock exchange like a share. Big brokers create and redeem its shares in blocks, and the daily flow numbers measure exactly those creations and redemptions.

title: What is Base? How Coinbase's $14.7B layer 2 works and who can change it
dek: Base is an Ethereum layer 2, an optimistic rollup built with the OP Stack, and the biggest by value: about $14.7 billion secured as of November 2, 2026, per L2BEAT. It runs transactions cheaply, posts the data to Ethereum, and a Coinbase multisig holds one of its two upgrade keys.

title: What is proof of reserves? What it proves about exchanges, and what it misses
dek: Proof of reserves is a public check that an exchange holds at least as much crypto as its customers have deposited. Merkle trees or zero-knowledge proofs let you confirm your balance was counted, but it is a one-day snapshot, not proof the company is solvent.

title: What is x402? The HTTP payment protocol that lets AI agents pay per request
dek: x402 is an open protocol that uses the web's "402 Payment Required" status code so apps and AI agents can pay for an API call or a web page in stablecoins, inside the request itself, with no account or card form.

title: Asian exchanges lost $11.95 billion in three weeks, most of it USDT leaving Binance
dek: DeepSea's data shows a steady stablecoin exodus from Asian exchanges starting September 28, weeks before Binance was hacked. Western exchanges barely moved, while smaller dollar tokens began to swing.

title: 12,562 sells, 10,480 buys: what Asia's crypto influencers really did in early October
dek: DeepSea's Asian KOL reports show influencer wallets selling more than they bought, a handful of traders taking most of the profit, and a quiet mid-October week on Solana. For followers, that is a warning.

title: Concrete's CT token fell 78% in a month. Its vaults still hold $1.2 billion
dek: Blueprint Finance's vault platform launched CT on September 30. By November 2 the token traded near $0.134, far below its $0.62 high, even though deposits held steady. Insiders and the foundation own 65% of supply, and its launch post gives no unlock dates.

title: A 100/100 token with bundlers among its top holders: how to read DeepSea's risk flags
dek: DeepSea checks every tracked token for holder concentration, thin liquidity, team selling and bundled supply. After October's run of drains and fake apps, here is what those signals mean, with real examples, and why one score is never the whole story.

title: Ether ETFs lost a record $1.61 billion in October, wiping out all of 2026's inflows
dek: US spot ether funds had their worst month since launch, beating November 2025's record outflow. October erased August and September's gains and left the funds slightly negative for the year, while ETH slid to about $2,270.

title: Sui promised Hashi in October with $500 million pledged. Its own page still says testnet
dek: Hashi is Sui's plan to let native bitcoin back loans on Sui. The Sui Foundation said mainnet would go live in October. On November 2, the official Hashi page still read "Now on Sui Testnet".

title: BlackRock's BUIDL slips to No. 3 as tokenized Treasuries shrink to $14.2 billion
dek: BlackRock's on-chain fund held $2.08 billion on November 1, down 7.61% in a month, and now ranks behind Ondo's USDY and Circle's USYC. The whole tokenized Treasury market shrank 3.68%, but holder numbers keep rising.

title: What is Hyperliquid? How the $188B-a-month onchain perps exchange works
dek: Hyperliquid is a blockchain built for trading. Its HyperCore engine runs perpetual futures and spot order books fully onchain, and DefiLlama showed $188.1 billion of perp volume in the 30 days to November 2, 2026.

title: MiCA explained: the EU crypto law, CASP licenses, stablecoin rules and key dates
dek: MiCA is the EU's rulebook for crypto: firms that offer crypto services need a license from a national regulator, and stablecoins face strict reserve and supervision rules. It has applied in full since December 30, 2024, and the last transition window closed on July 1, 2026.

title: What is Ethena USDe? How the hedged synthetic dollar works and what can break it
dek: USDe is Ethena's synthetic dollar. It is backed by crypto and stablecoins, with the crypto's price risk canceled out by short futures, and its staked version, sUSDe, earns from that trade until funding rates turn against it.

title: Base's next upgrade makes blocks 10 times faster. The code says November 5
dek: Coinbase's layer 2 switched on its Cobalt upgrade on September 30. Next is Denim, which cuts block times from 2 seconds to 200 milliseconds and could break contracts that count time in blocks. Base's code sets November 5, 1:00 p.m. ET, though Base still calls November only a target.

title: Brazil's crypto license deadline has passed. From November 6, banks must drop unlicensed firms
dek: Crypto firms already operating in Brazil had until October 30, 2026, to file for central bank authorization. From November 6, banks and payment firms may no longer deal with unauthorized providers, and late filers get 30 days at most.

title: Whales sold $22.8 million of UNI while it rose 7%, and bought LINK and ARB
dek: Big wallets used the late October bounce to sell, not buy. DeepSea's 7-day data shows whales net selling RLUSD, UNI and PEPE and making only small purchases of LINK and ARB, as bitcoin closed below $78,000 on October 29.

title: Hyperliquid's big traders flipped from 4.2x long to net short, then swung back to 86% long
dek: In mid-October, traders tracked by DeepSea dumped their bullish bets and piled into ETH and BTC shorts worth more than $200 million apiece. Two weeks later they were leaning long again, even as prices kept sliding.

title: Beyond Binance: 19 more crypto hacks in October's last 11 days, about $24.6 million lost
dek: Binance's $6.3 billion breach dominated October, but SlowMist logged 19 other attacks from October 21 to 31, close to two a day. They range from a $7.45 million multisig mistake to supply chain and DNS attacks.

title: What is Uniswap? How the $5.75B DEX works, from AMM pools to v4 hooks
dek: Uniswap is a decentralized exchange where people swap tokens against pools of liquidity instead of an order book. DefiLlama counted about $5.75 billion locked in it on November 2, 2026, and its newest version, v4, lets developers attach custom code called hooks to each pool.

title: Asian exchanges lost $2.2 billion in one week, and $2.12 billion of it left Binance
dek: DeepSea's report for October 12 to 18 shows stablecoins, mostly USDT on Tron, pouring out of Binance while bitcoin flowed in. The same week, hack-linked funds flooded exchange deposit addresses and a few big Hyperliquid traders turned short.

title: GENIUS Act explained: what the US stablecoin law requires and who enforces it
dek: The GENIUS Act is the US federal law for payment stablecoins. It requires full reserves, quick redemption and no interest for simply holding a token, and it takes effect on January 18, 2027, under the OCC's final rule.

title: What is Aave? How the $10.9B DeFi lending protocol works and what can go wrong
dek: Aave is a set of smart contracts where people supply crypto to earn interest and borrow against collateral, with no bank in the middle. As of November 2, 2026, DefiLlama counted about $10.9 billion locked in it, most of it on Ethereum.

title: Smart money net bought $1.09 million of Concrete as it slid 17%. Its top sale: AUSD
dek: DeepSea's seven-day flow data to November 2 shows tracked smart money wallets building a position in Concrete (CT) while its price fell, and pulling $3.77 million out of the AUSD stablecoin. Selling signals outnumbered buying ones.

title: Pump.fun added Monad and TON and is pushing perps. So why is PUMP down 25% since October 12?
dek: The Solana memecoin app now lets users trade Monad and TON tokens from one USDC balance and is pushing leveraged perps. Its PUMP token kept sliding, and daily revenue fell about 35% in 11 days.

title: Aave V3.8 vote: 381,439 AAVE for, zero against, a new lock on 15 networks
dek: Aave Labs wants a reentrancy guard on every active Aave V3 market, built so flash loans and liquidations still work. AAVE holders backed it with zero AAVE against in a Snapshot vote that closed October 31; audits come before the final onchain step.

title: Code is not a shield: the FCA's draft crypto map covers DeFi, comments due November 18
dek: The UK regulator wants views by November 18, 2026, on draft guidance about when DeFi, stablecoin payments, market making and tech services need a license. Using smart contracts does not settle the question on its own.
